introduction: Bram has caught you at the fence line the evening before the Public Farm. He calls it a courtesy. He has clearly rehearsed it, and he is going to get all the way to the end of it before he notices what he has said.
introductionSummary: The evening before the floor, Bram delivers a rehearsed courtesy at the fence and does not survive being asked one question.

logicalFallacies.explanation: Answering the animal instead of the argument. Six weeks on the farm is a fact about Rue, not about the water.
Treating a count of who agreed as a reason. Forty-one animals agreeing is forty-one animals agreeing.

sentences.text: Rue. A courtesy, before Sunday. The motion is going up whatever either of us does about it.
Forty-one of the Meadow-Born have already said yes, and forty-one is not a mistake.

logicalFallacies.explanation: It counts agreement and treats the count as the argument. None of the forty-one is claimed to have looked at anything.

sentences.text: You would be standing up against the whole meadow, and you have been here six weeks.

logicalFallacies.explanation: Six weeks is a fact about Rue. It is offered as the reason he should sit down, which is not a reason about the pond.

statement.summary: The rehearsed courtesy: the count is settled, the meadow is unanimous, and Rue has not been here long enough to disagree.

options.reason: You answered a crowd with a smaller crowd. Once the question is whose animals are better animals, you have picked the one contest you cannot win.
options.summary: You counter forty-one with three, which concedes that counting was the right way to settle it.

sentences.text: Everyone on the hauling crew thinks it is the grate. That is three of us, and we are the ones who carry the water.

logicalFallacies.explanation: It answers a headcount with a headcount. Three haulers agreeing is no more a finding about water than forty-one Meadow-Born agreeing.

options.reason: A fair question, and he will answer it honestly, and it will not help. You have accepted that the vote is what settles what is in the pond.
options.summary: You query the arithmetic of the majority, which keeps the argument on headcounts.

sentences.text: Is forty-one a majority, though? How many animals are on this farm altogether?

options.reason: Names both moves — the crowd and the newcomer jab — as things that are not about the water, then offers a check anybody can run before dark. Bram concedes the grate on the record.
options.summary: You set both of his moves aside and offer him a walk to the outflow with your case staked on it.

unlockedSentences.text: You said forty-one agreed, and you said I have been here six weeks. Neither of those is about the water. So let us do the one that is: come to the outflow with me now, and if the grate is not bent I will drop the whole thing before Sunday.

sentences.text: Three haulers against forty-one. Thank you, Rue, you have just made my argument for me and saved me saying it.

statement.summary: He takes the smaller number gratefully, because the argument he wanted was always about numbers.

sentences.text: More than forty-one, I should think. But they did not turn up, did they, and the ones who turn up are the ones who count.

statement.summary: He answers honestly, shrugs off the rest of the farm for not attending, and nothing has moved.

sentences.text: It is bent. It has been bent since before the frost, and I have known that the whole time, and that does not mean the newcomers are not also — look. Take it up with Tobias.

statement.summary: He concedes it without going anywhere, tries to keep the other half of his case, and gives up halfway through.

sentences.text: Sunday, then. Duchess has the floor and Tobias speaks first, and he will be very kind to you about it.
And Rue — he is a great deal better at this than I am. I only have to be believed by animals who already like me, and there are not many.

statement.summary: He sets the order of Sunday, warns that Tobias is the better hand at it, and says something sadder than he means to.

A **[accent]real debate[/accent]**, just a very short one. The **[accent]moderator[/accent]** is live again.
